bear_case.summary: LULU at ~7.6x P/E looks optically cheap, but the core Americas franchise is shrinking (Americas comps -12%, US revenue -8%), guidance has been cut twice (FY revenue now -5% to -7%), and the Q2 EPS beat relied on a one-time $134.5M tariff refund. Brand erosion vs Alo/Vuori, tariff exposure and growing dependence on China make the low multiple potentially deserved.

thesis_breaking_risks.evidence: Q2 US revenue $1,302M vs $1,415M (-8%); Americas comps -12% (secondary).
thesis_breaking_risks.likelihood: High that declines continue near term
thesis_breaking_risks.early_warning_signal: Americas comps in Q3 (2026-12-03), markdown levels, holiday traffic

thesis_breaking_risks.evidence: China Mainland H1 revenue $885M vs $761M (+16%) - now the growth engine; geopolitics/consumer risk.
Inventory $1,711M at 2026-08-02 vs $1,701M at 2026-02-01 while revenue declines.
thesis_breaking_risks.early_warning_signal: Inventory growth vs sales growth gap; gross margin markdown commentary

accounting_quality_red_flags: Q2 gross margin 60.5% vs 58.5% (computed) flattered by one-time tariff refund - underlying margin lower.
Two guidance cuts in one year - management visibility poor.
value_trap_assessment: Earnings are declining (H1 net income $524M vs $685M, -24%); a low P/E on falling earnings with structural brand share loss in its largest market is a textbook value trap until Americas comps stabilize.
